title: Git Command Best Practices - Avoiding cmdand dquote> Lock

issue_encountered.problem: cmdand dquote> process lock during git commit
issue_encountered.description: When using complex multi-line commit messages with quotes in git commands, the process can lock up with 'cmdand dquote>' prompt, requiring manual intervention to exit
issue_encountered.root_cause: Complex multi-line commit messages with nested quotes can confuse the shell parser
issue_encountered.impact: Blocks deployment process, requires manual intervention, delays milestone pushes

solution_implemented.pattern: git commit -m "🚀 MILESTONE: Brief descriptive message"
solution_implemented.avoid: Multi-line commit messages with complex formatting
solution_implemented.benefit: Clean, fast commits without shell parsing issues

best_practices: Keep git commit messages simple and single-line
Avoid nested quotes in commit messages
Use emojis for visual clarity without complexity
Test commit commands before running in deployment scripts
Have fallback commit message templates ready
deployment_script_requirements: Validate commit message format before execution
Include error handling for git operations
Test git commands in isolated environment first
Document all git command patterns used
lessons_learned: Shell parsing can be unpredictable with complex strings
Simple is better than complex for deployment automation
Always test git commands before including in scripts
Keep deployment processes robust and predictable
Document bad practices to prevent recurrence
prevention_measures: Added to deployment script requirements and collective memory
